overview: White plays 3.f4 against the French, building an e5/f4 chain or a Stonewall-like set-up without committing to the main theory. Black usually replies 3...Nf6 4.e5 Nfd7 or 3...dxe4, and plays against the centre with ...c5 and ...Nc6. White aims for a kingside attack with Nf3, Bd3 and O-O. It is a rare, system-like sideline and I know it only roughly.

white_ideas.idea: Advance e5 and support it with f4
Develop Nf3, Bd3, O-O and attack on the kingside

black_ideas.idea: Take on e4 and trade pieces

typical_structures.structure: Closed centre where play shifts to the wings

character.notes: Closed and slow with a possible kingside attack; not particularly sharp.

gambit.notes: No material is given in the main lines.

soundness.notes: Probably sound but slightly worse for White than the main lines.

structure.notes: If Black plays ...Nf6, e5 follows and the centre locks.

level.notes: Plans are clear, but the light-squared bishop and ...c5 break need care.

character.reason: Thin evidence; semi-closed with attacking chances for White.

plans.reason: e5/f4 space and a kingside plan.
